Current allocation: 'EU1 (AlphaVPS, Bulgaria): 10/10 VMs Allocated (0 slots free)' and 'US1 (VirMach, New York): 10/10 VMs Allocated (0 slots free)'.

per_object_cap.stated: '10/10 VMs Allocated (0 slots free)' on both hosts, so there is no free slot to allocate today

retention.stated: not published as a clock; the project states applicants are 'Expected to have a purpose in mind to use the service (no idlers)'

record.interface_detail: a KVM virtual machine with root, one IPv4, on a host donated by AlphaVPS in Sofia or VirMach in New York
record.chaining: Nothing until a slot frees: both hosts are at 10 of 10.

limits.value: 2 vCPU, 2 GB RAM, 25 GB SSD on EU1; 2 vCPU, 3 GB RAM, 120 GB HDD on US1
a forum account at least 3 months old, a FraudRecord check, and a human review of the application

record.binding_note: Capacity is the first wall and reputation is the second: both hosts report 0 of 10 slots free, and the application requires a three-month-old forum account that passes a FraudRecord check.

identity_cost.detail: no card, but a reputation gate: quoted 'Must be an active user of LowEndSpirit, HostedTalk, and/or LowEndTalk communities'; 'LES/HT/LET account must be at least 3 months old at time of application'; 'Must pass a FraudRecord check (Do not use a proxy to submit the application)'. The application is a Google Form.

record.reliability_note: No reliability event observed. The project publishes a status link to a HetrixTools monitor.
record.confidence_note: The allocation count, the specification and the eligibility rules are quoted from the project's own page read. The page is small and the project is one person's, so this is documented about the offer and about the current full capacity.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'EU1 (AlphaVPS, Bulgaria): 10/10 VMs Allocated (0 slots free)', 'US1 (VirMach, New York): 10/10 VMs Allocated (0 slots free)'; 'LES/HT/LET account must be at least 3 months old at time of application'; 'Must pass a FraudRecord check'; specs '2 vCPU', '2GB RAM', '25GB SSD', '1TB @ 1 Gbps', '1 IPv4'

record.notes: A real project with real sponsors and a real specification, documented because it is the clearest illustration of why the free-VPS forum layer is not a route: every slot is full, and the door is a three-month-old forum account plus a fraud check. earlier readings already carries freevps.org and microlxc on the same reputation model. Nothing here is a defect in the project; it is simply not available to a person who is not already in that community.

extras.price_arithmetic: no charge; the constraint is eligibility and capacity, not price

network_out.ports: 1 IPv4, 1 TB a month at 1 Gbps

session_cap.note: no clock published; 'no idlers' is the stated policy

record.provider: FreeMach — community free VPS (LES/HT/LET members, 3-month account age)

free_tier.stated: US1.KVM: 2 vCPU, 3 GB RAM, 120 GB HDD, 1 TB transfer. EU1.KVM: 2 vCPU, 2 GB, 25 GB SSD, 1 TB. Hosts are a VirMach Buffalo E3-1240v3 with 2x1TB HDD and an AlphaVPS Sofia dual-L5630.

egress.terms: 1 TB per VM at 1 Gbps. Metered and small.

record.chaining: Hard-gated on community standing, not on payment: 'LES/HT/LET account must be at least 3 months old at time of application', 'Must pass a FraudRecord check (Do not use a proxy to submit the application)'. That check is a risk-scoring screen. A second account would need an aged forum identity and a clean risk-scoring record, which is the actual scarce resource.
record.limits_note: 120 GB max disk per VM, 1 TB transfer. Currently 0 slots: 'EU1 (AlphaVPS, Bulgaria): 10/10 VMs Allocated (0 slots free) … US1 (VirMach, New York): 10/10 VMs Allocated (0 slots free)'.
record.reliability_note: Sponsored capacity on other people's dedicated servers, 10 VMs per node. The risk-scoring screen means a closure follows the person across the low-end host ecosystem. That is the strongest usage-anomaly signal in the niche.

evidence.proved: 'Must be an active user of LowEndSpirit, HostedTalk, and/or LowEndTalk … at least 3 months old'; 'Must pass a FraudRecord check (Do not use a proxy to submit the application)'; '10/10 VMs Allocated (0 slots free)' on both nodes. The check the page names is a risk-scoring screen.

record.notes: US1.KVM: 2 vCPU, 3 GB RAM, 120 GB HDD, 1 TB transfer. EU1.KVM: 2 vCPU, 2 GB, 25 GB SSD, 1 TB. Hosts are a VirMach Buffalo E3-1240v3 with 2x1TB HDD and an AlphaVPS Sofia dual-L5630.
